candidates.name: Syphilis
support_spans: Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutiation assay: positive
Rapid plasma reagin testing: 1:64 titer
Direct scrapings from skin plaques demonstrate interface dermatitis with spirochetes evident upon hematoxylin-eosin staining
candidates.why: The patient's positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay, rapid plasma reagin testing, and skin lesion histopathology demonstrating spirochetes are indicative of syphilis.

candidates.name: Ocular Syphilis
support_spans: bilateral photophobia and decreased vision
vitreous cell and haze obscuring retinal vascular details, blurred disc margins, and superonasal peripheral retinal whitening
disc leakage and superotemporal staining of an area of retinitis
candidates.why: The patient's ocular symptoms and findings are consistent with ocular syphilis, a known complication of syphilis.

candidates.why: The patient's low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level indicate significant immunosuppression, which increases the risk of opportunistic infections such as syphilis and ocular syphilis.
